program_name: Nebraska Homeless Assistance Program (NHAP) Legal Services (DHHS RFA 4533)
program_date_basis: RFA released 2025-04-22 and applications closed 2025-05-21, both printed in the RFA itself
disqualifying_fact: Nebraska DHHS RFA 4533 says the department is "awarding state funds to an eligible and qualified agency to provide legal services" for the Nebraska Homeless Assistance Program, a HUD/ESG-linked homelessness programme ($15,000 over three years). STATE money, not RHTP. The dates close it independently: applications closed 2025-05-21, seven months before CMS issued Nebraska its RHTP Notice of Award on 2025-12-29. This is the programme behind RCJ's single Nebraska Lawyers Foundation Tier 3 candidate. THIS ROW MATCHES NO CANDIDATE TODAY AND THAT IS THE POINT OF IT. The sweep's provenance text is the source-document title plus the solicitation number, and RCJ's title for that row is the bare string "Intent to Award" with no programme identifier and no solicitation number at all -- so no source-scoped registry entry can reach it, and the date test cannot run either because RCJ carries no date for it (15 of Nebraska's 39 candidates are undatable). The automated sweep therefore caught ZERO Nebraska rows while a non-RHTP row was sitting in the candidate set; it was found by hand, by checking the name against the state's three notices of award. Nebraska's clean sweep line was a statement about the registry's coverage, not about Nebraska. The row is disposed of in ne_rcj_candidate_disposition.csv; this entry is kept so that the NEXT Nebraska candidate whose title does name NHAP or RFA 4533 is caught by machine rather than by luck.

program_name: Nevada Graduate Medical Education (GME) Grant Program, Round VIII (NVHA)
match_regex: GME Grant Program|GME Grant Round|Grant Round VIII|Train the Next Generation of Physicians
program_date_basis: announcement dated 2026-07-22, printed on the release itself
disqualifying_fact: Nevada's Graduate Medical Education Grant Program is STATE GENERAL FUND money. NVHA's own April 2026 workforce publication prints GME, WRRAP and SHARP side by side under a column headed "Funding" and gives each one's source: GME is "Source: State General Fund" governed by NRS 223.631-639 and SB262 & SB494 (2025); WRRAP is "Source: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Grant #RHTCMS332074-01-02"; SHARP is "Source: SB5 one-time bill appropriation". ONLY WRRAP IS RHTP. The 2026-07-22 release announcing Round VIII's $15,755,068.00 to nine residency and fellowship programmes calls them "these new state investments" and mentions neither CMS nor RHTP anywhere. SEVENTEEN of RCJ's 34 Nevada Tier 3 candidates are those nine awards, carried twice under two RHTP-titled documents. THE LESSON IS THAT THE CMS FINANCIAL-ASSISTANCE FOOTER IS NOT A PROVENANCE TEST ON ITS OWN: the workforce publication carries that footer on EVERY PAGE -- "$179,931,608.42 with 100% funded by CMS/HHS" -- because NVHA produced the publication with RHTP money, while two of the three programmes it describes are state-funded. Oklahoma's footer sat on a ROSTER and covered what was on it; Nevada's sits on a COMPARISON DOCUMENT and covers only the publishing. A check keyed on the footer passes all seventeen of these rows. What disqualifies them is the funding-source line, and the date test does not reach them either -- Round VIII is a 2026 award, well after the 2025-12-29 Notice of Award, so it is NOT PROVENANCE_PREDATES_NOA. This is Texas's Rider 88 in a state whose documents are otherwise impeccable. WHAT THIS ROW ACTUALLY CATCHES IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: keyed on the GME release's own title it reaches 9 of the 17 rows, with ZERO false positives inside Nevada and none possible outside it (rhtp_match_state_program() filters the registry by state first). The other 8 are filed by RCJ under "Nevada Home Working Together RHTP 2026 Award Announcement" -- the workforce publication, which IS a genuine RHTP document -- so no source-title-keyed rule can honestly reach them and they are disposed of by hand in nv_rcj_candidate_disposition.csv. The regex is deliberately NOT the bare phrase "Graduate Medical Education": that matches three real GEORGIA rural hospital awards of $500,000 each whose Dual Track grant titles contain it, and -- more to the point inside Nevada -- it would match NVHA's own RHTP release, which funds "a new statewide Rural Graduate Medical Education Consortium" with WRRAP money.

program_name: Michigan MDHHS youth substance-use prevention grants (opioid settlement funded)
match_regex: prevent substance use among Michigan youth|opioid settlement
program_date_basis: MDHHS newsroom release date, read out of the archived page rather than typed.
disqualifying_fact: MDHHS's own sub-headline states the funding source: "New opioid settlement-funded grants support 12 organizations". The release awards nearly $3.75 million to 12 organizations for youth substance-use prevention and the words "Rural Health Transformation", "RHTP" and "rural" appear ZERO times in it. RCJ files eight of the twelve as Michigan RHTP Tier 3 candidates. THE FIRST ALTERNATIVE IS WHAT DOES THE WORK AND IT CATCHES ALL EIGHT: RCJ carries the release HEADLINE ("MDHHS awards nearly $3.75 million to help prevent substance use among Michigan youth") as its source-document title, so the sweep reaches these rows on the headline even though the funding source is in the SUB-headline, which RCJ does not carry. The "opioid settlement" alternative matches nothing today and is registered anyway, on Nebraska's RFA 4533 precedent: an alternative that matches nothing now is what catches the next candidate whose title does name the funding stream.
